_meta.purpose: Questions that must be answered before a decision is reasonable, given what we do and do not know. Each entry states what we know now, what is missing, why the gap blocks a decision, and the cheapest way to close it.
_meta.convention: Blocks a decision = you cannot sensibly choose between the options in suggestions.json until this is answered. Does not block = useful context, but you can proceed without it.

questions.question: Is the Associates account for shopnow047c-20 currently enrolled and in good standing?
questions.what_we_know: The tag format (XXXXX-##) matches the pattern Amazon describes in Program Policies §2(b).
questions.what_is_missing: Enrollment status, account country/store, and whether the account has ever recorded a click. None of this is visible without signing in to Associates Central.
questions.why_it_matters: If the account is not approved, every link on this site earns nothing and the entire build is premature. This is the single highest-value unknown on the page.
questions.how_to_close: Sign in to affiliate-program.amazon.com → Account Settings. Record the tag exactly as shown and the enrollment date.

questions.question: Do the five supplied link.amazon short links actually credit shopnow047c-20?
questions.what_we_know: All five resolve to the correct ASINs. None of the observed landing URLs contains a tag= parameter; they carry a page-share token (btn_ref=srctok-…).
questions.what_is_missing: Whether link.amazon resolves the tag server-side, or whether the link was generated as a plain share rather than a Special Link.
questions.why_it_matters: Amazon's Commission Income Statement pays on clicks through a Special Link. If these are untagged shares, no session is created. This is not a claim that the links are broken — it is an unresolved fact.
questions.how_to_close: The enrolled-workflow test described in Q03 settles it definitively.

questions.question: Have these links been tested end-to-end in the enrolled Associates workflow — click, then confirm the destination and the click in the tracking report?
questions.what_we_know: No. Nothing in the supplied material shows a test result.
questions.what_is_missing: One click per product, then a look at Reports → Link Type / Tracking ID for that day.
questions.why_it_matters: This is the only way to confirm attribution without guessing at link internals. One product is enough to start; scale only after it reports.
questions.how_to_close: Click product 1 from a phone on cellular, wait 24-48h, check the Associates click report for the tag.

questions.question: Should outbound links use amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=shopnow047c-20 directly instead of the link.amazon short form?
questions.what_we_know: Program Policies §2(b) says the tag must appear as a parameter in the URL of each link.
questions.what_is_missing: Whether the owner's enrolled workflow produces links the owner can regenerate with the tag visible.
questions.why_it_matters: A visible tag parameter makes the whole question auditable and removes the guesswork in Q02. It is the simplest possible fix if the short links turn out to be untagged.
questions.how_to_close: In SiteStripe or the product page's 'Get Link' dialog, generate one text link and note whether the URL contains tag=shopnow047c-20.

questions.question: Which Amazon store is the account enrolled in — amazon.com only, or several?
questions.what_we_know: Every supplied link points to amazon.com (US).
questions.what_is_missing: The store list in the account settings.
questions.why_it_matters: It determines whether a UK or Canadian reader can be served at all, and whether the disclosure wording needs a store name.
questions.how_to_close: Account Settings → account country / store list.

questions.question: Does the owner hold the rights to use any manufacturer imagery, and do we want to?
questions.what_we_know: The site currently uses zero third-party images — only CSS-drawn cards and typographic treatments.
questions.what_is_missing: Whether PA API image access is available; whether the owner wants real photography badly enough to obtain licensed assets.
questions.why_it_matters: A shopping site without product images converts worse, but pulled Amazon images require API compliance and pulled manufacturer images require permission. This is the main visual-quality constraint.
questions.how_to_close: Apply for PA API / Creators API access and read the IP License; or commission original photography of owned units.

questions.question: Is API access (PA API or Creators API) approved for this account?
questions.what_we_know: No API credentials exist in this repo and none were used. All data was read from public product pages.
questions.what_is_missing: Approval status. PA API requires qualifying sales before access.
questions.why_it_matters: API access is the only compliant route to showing live prices and availability (S03), and the only compliant route to product images (Q06). It unlocks the biggest quality jump available.
questions.how_to_close: Associates Central → Tools → Product Advertising API; check approval and quota.

questions.question: Will the site stay on github.io, or move to a real domain?
questions.what_we_know: GitHub Pages is live at https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/WinA/. Page source is main / root.
questions.what_is_missing: Budget, appetite for DNS, and whether a brand domain exists.
questions.why_it_matters: Search engines treat a github.io path as a shared domain with weak topical identity. A brand domain is the single biggest SEO lever available and it also fixes the canonical/sitemap host permanently.
questions.how_to_close: Decide domain or no domain, then either add a CNAME file or accept the github.io origin.

questions.question: Where will analytics actually run, given Pages is static?
questions.what_we_know: No analytics endpoint exists. The event layer is written and disabled. GitHub Pages cannot execute server code.
questions.what_is_missing: A choice between a hosted privacy-friendly provider, a separate small host for the endpoint, or no analytics at all.
questions.why_it_matters: Until this is answered, the campaign ledger stays empty and topic selection stays instinct-driven. Measurement was requested as priority zero, and it is the one thing the current stack cannot self-host.
questions.how_to_close: Pick one: Plausible/Umami cloud, a Cloudflare Worker or VPS endpoint, or self-host on a second host.

questions.question: Do we have first-hand access to any of these five products?
questions.what_we_know: No. Nothing on this site claims hands-on testing, and no first-person experience is asserted anywhere.
questions.what_is_missing: Whether the owner owns, can borrow, or will buy any of the units.
questions.why_it_matters: It is the difference between a specification comparison and a review. It also determines whether words like 'we tested' may ever appear — right now they may not.
questions.how_to_close: Owner decision: buy one unit, or accept that the site is a documented comparison site and never implies testing.

questions.question: Is there search demand for these specific questions, or are we guessing?
questions.what_we_know: Four question-shaped guide titles were supplied as editorial hypotheses. They are explicitly working titles, not claims about search volume.
questions.what_is_missing: Any keyword volume, SERP competition or Search Console query data.
questions.why_it_matters: Publishing cadence is cheap; publishing into zero-demand queries is not free, it costs the time budget. Even a free keyword source would convert the guide list from hypothesis to plan.
questions.how_to_close: After Search Console is live, choose topics from the Queries report instead of from instinct.

questions.question: Who is the reader — a first-time air fryer buyer, or someone upgrading?
questions.what_we_know: The three air fryers span 6 qt dual-basket, 8 qt single-basket and a 26 qt oven. That is a spread across three buyer types, not one.
questions.what_is_missing: A chosen primary audience for the front page.
questions.why_it_matters: The front page currently ranks the three by 'who it suits' rather than by a single best pick, because choosing one pick would require knowing the audience.
questions.how_to_close: Owner picks one primary reader. Then the front page can lead with one recommendation instead of three.

questions.question: How current do the specification rows need to be, and who refreshes them?
questions.what_we_know: Every value carries an observation timestamp of 2026-11-20. Star ratings and review counts change daily.
questions.what_is_missing: A refresh owner and a refresh interval.
questions.why_it_matters: Stale specs on an affiliate site are both a UX problem and a compliance risk under S04. A documented interval is cheaper than a rewrite.
questions.how_to_close: Decide 30-day or 90-day refresh and name the owner.

questions.question: Which five events count as the measurement set?
questions.what_we_know: An event schema is defined: product_view, outbound_click, disclosure_view, compare_open, guide_read_complete.
questions.what_is_missing: Confirmation that these five are the intended five.
questions.why_it_matters: Events are cheap to fire and expensive to define later. Changing the schema after launch fragments the data.
questions.how_to_close: Owner confirms or edits the five event names.

questions.question: What is the definition of an 'eligible session' for the campaign ledger?
questions.what_we_know: The ledger defines eligible_session as a session in which the landing page rendered and the disclosure strip was in the viewport at least once.
questions.what_is_missing: Owner agreement on that definition, plus the cookie/session boundary.
questions.why_it_matters: Without a fixed definition, click-through rate is not comparable month to month and the ledger becomes decorative.
questions.how_to_close: Owner signs off on the definition in data/ledger.json.

questions.question: Will reported orders come from Amazon's Associates report or from somewhere else?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing. The ledger's orders field is null and must stay null until an authorized first-party report supplies a number.
questions.what_is_missing: Which report, which date range, and who transcribes it.
questions.why_it_matters: Mixing self-estimated orders with reported orders destroys the only trustworthy number the project will have.
questions.how_to_close: On first payout cycle, export the Associates order report and paste the period totals with the export date.

questions.question: Does the publication need a name and masthead, or is 'WinA' acceptable?
questions.what_we_know: 'WinA' is the repository name. A publication masthead was requested; the site currently uses a descriptive name and a typographic masthead.
questions.what_is_missing: Owner decision on the name, and a trademark check on whatever name is chosen.
questions.why_it_matters: Program Policies §1(g) forbids Amazon trademarks or near-misspellings in a domain or brand name. A name chosen without that check can disqualify the site outright.
questions.how_to_close: Pick a name, then check it against Amazon's Non-Exhaustive Trademark Table and a USPTO search before buying a domain.

questions.question: Is the category list frozen at two, or should the site expand to adjacent kitchen categories?
questions.what_we_know: Five products across two categories: air fryers (3) and thermometers (2).
questions.what_is_missing: Whether more ASINs will be supplied.
questions.why_it_matters: Two categories is thin for a publication front page but fine for a focused buying guide. Adding categories before adding depth would produce the thin-content problem the site is trying to avoid.
questions.how_to_close: Owner supplies more ASINs or confirms scope is closed.

questions.question: Is a privacy policy needed, and does the analytics choice change the answer?
questions.what_we_know: The site sets no cookies by default and ships analytics disabled.
questions.what_is_missing: The jurisdiction served, and the final analytics choice.
questions.why_it_matters: Enabling any endpoint changes what must be disclosed. The current build is deliberately cookie-free so the question can be deferred, not ignored.
questions.how_to_close: Answer after Q09.

questions.question: Who reviews flagged items, and how often?
questions.what_we_know: Ten flags are published on the Flagged for Review page.
questions.what_is_missing: A review owner and a cadence.
questions.why_it_matters: Flags that are never reviewed are just a longer way of saying 'we don't know'. The page exists to be emptied.
questions.how_to_close: Owner sets a weekly 15-minute review slot.

questions.question: Do we want Cloudflare or similar in front of Pages for redirects and the analytics endpoint?
questions.what_we_know: Pages serves the site; no redirect layer exists.
questions.what_is_missing: Willingness to add a third party.
questions.why_it_matters: It would solve the analytics-endpoint problem and the www/non-www problem without leaving static hosting.
questions.how_to_close: Decide alongside Q09 and Q08.

questions.question: Are we allowed to describe the Emeril unit as rotisserie-capable, given the page's own numbers disagree?
questions.what_we_know: The title says 26QT / 24 presets, a bullet says 25 presets, the spec table says 24.6 L. The page states a 6-lb chicken rotisserie capacity.
questions.what_is_missing: Which figure is correct, and whether the accessories differ by variant.
questions.why_it_matters: S04 forbids inaccurate claims. Where the source contradicts itself, the safe move is to print the contradiction, which is what the site does today.
questions.how_to_close: Open the manufacturer's own page or manual for the exact model and compare.

questions.question: Does the site need to state a price-update disclaimer even though it prints no prices?
questions.what_we_know: No price appears anywhere. The policy only constrains showing price.
questions.what_is_missing: Whether the owner prefers a belt-and-braces 'prices change' line anyway.
questions.why_it_matters: A disclaimer about a number you never print can itself confuse the reader. The current choice is to explain why no price is shown instead.
questions.how_to_close: Owner preference.

questions.question: Is a parallel-session workflow still in use, or is this a single-maintainer repo now?
questions.what_we_know: COORDINATION.md defines a parallel-session protocol. One session did all the work this run.
questions.what_is_missing: Whether more sessions will run.
questions.why_it_matters: If it becomes single-maintainer, the protocol can shrink to a simple changelog, which is easier to keep honest.
questions.how_to_close: Owner confirms.
